offence_severity: imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life
physical_harm: death caused by administration of poison
number_of_offences: Four offences/counts charged, but only one was finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court did not accept the prosecution's reliance on the statements of PW3 and PW4, nor did it find the documentary evidence in the form of letters sufficient to prove the allegations of dowry-related cruelty and harassment soon before the deceased's death.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses' statements as insufficient and not corroborated by independent evidence, leading to the conclusion that the prosecution failed to establish the necessary elements of the offence under Section 304-B IPC.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 03.02.1994; Trial judgment: 12.12.1995; High Court decision: 21.01.2009; Supreme Court decision: 07.08.2019
legal_representation: D. N. Goburdhan, Adv. for the Appellant; Shekhar Raj Sharma, Vishwa Pal Singh, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered on 09.02.1994; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction of the appellant; High Court: Allowed appeal of Savitri Devi, acquitted her, reduced sentence of the appellant to seven years; Supreme Court: Set aside conviction of the appellant, set him at liberty
prosecution_argument: The prosecution relied on the statements of PW3 (father of the deceased) and PW4 (brother of the deceased), as well as letters written by the deceased, to establish that she was subjected to cruelty relating to dowry demands soon before her death. However, the court found these statements and letters insufficient to prove the necessary elements of the offense under Section 304-B IPC.
defence_argument: The defense argued that the prosecution failed to prove the essential ingredients of Section 304-B IPC, specifically that the deceased was subjected to cruelty or harassment related to dowry demands soon before her death. The defense emphasized the lack of independent evidence and the absence of proof regarding the timing of the alleged harassment.
legal_principle_applied: The court applied the principle that the prosecution must establish a proximate nexus between the deceased's death and the cruelty or harassment inflicted on her due to dowry demands, and that the term 'soon before her death' implies a close temporal relationship between the harassment and the death.
precedent_relied_upon: Satvir Singh & Ors. v. State of Punjab & Anr. (2001) 8 SCC 633; Hira Lal & Ors. v. State (Govt. of NCT), Delhi (2003) 8 SCC 80; Sakatar Singh & Ors. v. State of Haryana (2004) 11 SCC 291; Major Singh and Anr. v. State of Punjab (2015) 5 SCC 201
sentencing_rationale: The prosecution failed to prove the allegations against the appellant beyond reasonable doubt, and therefore, the conviction was set aside. The appellant was set at liberty as long as he is not involved in any other case.
